clue.text: Artillery stuck in Scottish bog, a swamp

indicators.note: something stuck in a thing is lodged inside it, so the first piece sits within the second

parts.note: in Scotland and northern England a moss is a peat bog
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Guns bogged down on a Scottish moor, the whole place a quagmire.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is an area of soft, wet, boggy ground, which is exactly what a swamp is.

clue.text: Pass an examination

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to overtake, as one vehicle passes another
second meaning: a thorough inspection and repair

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a student succeeding in a test; 'Pass' is really overtaking on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtake another vehicle is to pass it, and a full check of an engine or system is a thorough examination.

clue.text: Moving not a step before the race

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner on the start line, not shifting a step before the race begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Ante-post betting is a British racing term: bets placed in advance, before the runners are declared on race day.
explanation.definitionFit: Ante-post describes bets struck before the day of a race, so it means before the race.

clue.text: Lachesis used to be a raconteur

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a Fate of Greek myth at her work, spinning thread for each human life
setter's reading: tell long, entertaining stories

explanation.surface: The Greek Fate who spins the thread of life once told tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fates spun, measured and cut the thread of life; the same idiom covers that spinning and telling a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes, and to tell a long rambling story is the idiom here.

clue.text: Rex is written in italic letters

indicators.note: a word written in another is placed inside its letters

parts.note: italic type slopes, so it is leaning
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A note on typography: the word Rex printed in sloping italic type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italic letters' reads as one phrase about type, but italic is the wordplay and letters alone is the definition, in the sense of a man of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters in the sense of scholarship or erudition, as in a man of letters, means much the same as learning.

clue.text: Exotic island whereon to relax

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters come out in an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A faraway tropical island, the perfect place to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of 'island whereon to' are rearranged; 'to' does double duty in the surface but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop being formal and enjoy oneself freely, which is to relax.

clue.text: Dress torn, cut by intent

indicators.note: a word cut by another is split open with the other placed in the gap

parts.note: rent is an old past tense of rend, to tear
one's aim is one's intent

explanation.surface: A dress ripped and slashed on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torn' looks like an adjective describing the dress, but it stands for an old past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing, so it means dress in the sense of attire.

clue.text: Notorious assassin from Nurmes originally (in Finland) turning up

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means reading from bottom to top
a thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: Suomi is the Finnish name for Finland

indicators.note: originally points to how each word starts, so only its first letter counts

parts.note: the first letters of the three words; Nurmes is a town in Finland

explanation.surface: A notorious killer from a Finnish town surfaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' covers all three words before it, not just Nurmes, and the brackets mark where the letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamous means well known for something bad, which is exactly what notorious means.

clue.text: Frenchman climbs, smothered in hoary leaves

indicators.note: something smothered in another is wrapped up completely inside it

parts.note: hoary means grey or white with age

indicators.note: in a down answer, a word that climbs is read upwards, from last letter to first

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman climbing a frosty tree, buried among its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery means green foliage or vegetation, so leaves taken together as a mass.

clue.text: Bound to take it easy with damaged hearing

parts.note: to rest is to take it easy

indicators.note: hearing a word means taking it by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: ricked means sprained or wrenched, as in a ricked neck

explanation.surface: Someone with poor hearing confined to rest and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: To rick a joint is to sprain it, a British usage; RICKED said out loud gives the end of RESTRICT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound something is to set limits on it, so the verb means to confine or restrict.

clue.text: Rubbish heap split by two fellows

indicators.note: a thing split by something has that something pushed into its middle

parts.note: a pile is a heap
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two of them make FF

explanation.surface: A rubbish heap being divided up by a couple of men.
explanation.walkthrough: FF goes into the middle of PILE: PI-FF-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Piffle is nonsense, foolish talk, and rubbish is used in exactly that sense.

clue.text: Man buried by a padre

parts.note: a chap is a man
something buried has lain in the ground

explanation.surface: A man laid to rest by a priest at a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a burial service; 'buried' is a past participle swapped for LAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the forces' name for a clergyman attached to a regiment or ship, an army or navy chaplain.

clue.text: European composer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a native of Germany
second meaning: Sir Edward ..., English composer of light opera

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like one person described, but the two words are separate meanings; Edward German wrote the comic opera Merrie England.
explanation.definitionFit: A German is a person from Germany, so a European, and Edward German was a well-known English composer.

clue.text: Breaks stolen image

parts.note: something that breaks snaps
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a stolen picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quickly taken photograph, and a photograph is an image.

clue.text: Beyond control immediately

definitions.meaning: first meaning: unruly, no longer manageable
second meaning: at once, without further thought, as in dismissing an idea

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like something going wrong at once; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation that has got out of hand is uncontrolled, and rejecting a plan out of hand means doing so straight away.

clue.text: A sample of his laths

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion taken from something, so the letters are lifted from inside the words

explanation.surface: Someone shows off one of the thin wooden strips he owns.

explanation.definitionFit: A slat is a thin narrow strip of wood, which is what a lath is, so one is a fair sample.

clue.text: Geese ran wild, like Robespierre

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Geese stampeding, compared with a French revolutionary.

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle's famous epithet for the French revolutionary leader describes his greenish pallor, so he was sea-green.

clue.text: King in love, a king who offers protection

clue.text: Catch eastern agent

clue.text: Vision seen in a boat — O.K?

clue.text: Delve into foreign father with English ancestry

clue.text: Soldiers discover child by the railway

parts.note: an infant is a young child

clue.text: Rail — one given new shape, an H

indicators.note: a word given a new shape keeps its letters but takes a different form

parts.note: taken as written
the letter itself

clue.text: Enjoy oneself making love in a wood

clue.text: Relations experience rejection when female leaves to become dissident
